text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- No trucks with food or oil have entered Macedonia from Bulgaria in the past three days as Bulgarian customs strictly enforce measures taken by their government. On Monday only one thousand Macedonians crossed the Deve Bair border crossing to Bulgaria. Usually over 15,000 people cross.

- In an open letter to the Macedonian media U.N. special human rights rapporteur for the former Yugoslavia Elisabeth Rehn expressed disappointment with the way the Macedonian press had described her mission to the country and said higher education of national minorities was a serious problem.

- Some two thousand secondary school pupils and one hundred university students demonstrated on Tuesday in front of the government and parliament against a new law introducing Albanian-language classes in the Teachers' Academy.
- Macedonian students at the Teachers' Academy demand resignation of Education Minister Sofia Todorova.

- Macedonian Defence Minister Blagoja Handziski received on Monday the first Yugoslav military attache in Skopje colonel Predrag Stanisic. Both sides expressed readiness to determine the state border.
